fatal_errors: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is incorrectly treated as a refractory BCC/B2 alloy; the relevant as-cast eutectic alloy has an FCC+B2 lamellar constitution.
The proposed transition is aging-time-dependent at a fixed temperature, whereas the target transition is primarily temperature-dependent, with embrittlement near 600 °C and recovery near 750 °C.
Ordering is assigned to the B2 phase rather than enhanced L12 ordering within FCC domains.
The phase-fraction/percolation mechanism omits the essential jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries, stress concentration at their tips, planar slip, and suppression of cross-slip.
The VEC boundary conditions are unsupported by the cited evidence.
The proposed falsification experiment does not test crack initiation and dislocation pile-ups at jagged phase-boundary tips or exclude impurity-segregation-mediated embrittlement.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad question of a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile response during aging and invokes chemical ordering as a possible cause. However, it reconstructs a substantially different material system and mechanism. E1 directly identifies AlCoCrFeNi2.1 as an FCC/B2 eutectic alloy, contradicting the generated BCC/B2 description, while E2 and E3 concern refractory alloys and high-temperature BCC/B2 transformations that do not support behavior at 600–800 °C in AlCoCrFeNi2.1. The cited evidence also does not establish the proposed 10–100 hour kinetics, B2 phase-fraction percolation, VEC limits, or ductility recovery mechanism. Although the time-series tensile experiment could falsify the generated hypothesis, it would not discriminate the target mechanism because it lacks direct characterization of L12 ordering, phase-boundary morphology, localized dislocation behavior, crack initiation, and impurity segregation.
